arxiv-2203-16022.title: Emergence of classical spacetimes in canonical tensor model
arxiv-2203-16022.description: Abstract We study the wave function of a tensor model in the canonical formalism by Hamiltonian Monte Carlo method for Lie group symmetric or nearby values for the argument of the wave function, and show that there emerge Lie-group symmetric semi-classical spacetimes.

arxiv-2205-11595.title: From the origin of life to pandemics: Emergent phenomena in complex systems
arxiv-2205-11595.creator: Oriol Artime 1 and Manlio De Domenico 2
arxiv-2205-11595.description: Abstract When a large number of similar entities interact among each other and with their environment at a low scale, unexpected outcomes at higher spatio-temporal scales might spontaneously arise. This nontrivial phenomenon, known as emergence, characterizes a broad range of distinct complex systems – from physical to biological and social ones – and is often related to collective behavior.

arxiv-2210-09480.title: Photon Energy-Resolved Velocity Map Imaging from Spectral Domain Ghost Imaging
arxiv-2210-09480.creator: Jun Wang, Taran Driver, Felix Allum, Christina C. Papadopoulou, Christopher Passow, Günter Brenner, Siqi Li, Stefan Düsterer, Atia Tul Noor, Sonu Kumar, Philip H. Bucksbaum, Benjamin Erk, Ruaridh Forbes, James P. Cryan
arxiv-2210-09480.description: Abstract We present an approach that combines photon spectrum correlation analysis with the reconstruction of three-dimensional momentum distribution from velocity map images in an efficient, single-step procedure. We demonstrate its efficacy with the results from the photoionization of the 2 ​ p 2p -shell of argon using the FLASH free-electron laser (FEL).

arxiv-2301-04736.title: Twisted recurrence for dynamical systems with exponential decay of correlations
arxiv-2301-04736.description: Abstract We study the set of points returning infinitely often to a sequence of targets dependent on the starting points. With an assumption of decay of correlations for L 1 L^{1} against bounded variations, we prove a generalized quantitative recurrence result under Lipschitz twists.

arxiv-2303-10915.title: Free-induction-decay magnetic field imaging with a microfabricated Cs vapor cell Journal: opticajournal Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2303-10915.creator: Dominic Hunter, 1,* Chris Perrella, 2 Allan McWilliam, 1 James P. McGilligan, 1 Marcin Mrozowski, 1 Stuart J. Ingleby, 1 Paul F. Griffin, 1 David Burt, 3 Andre N. Luiten, 2 and Erling Riis 1
arxiv-2303-10915.description: Abstract Magnetic field imaging is a valuable resource for signal source localization and characterization. This work reports an optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) based on the free-induction-decay (FID) protocol, that implements microfabricated cesium (Cs) vapor cell technology to visualize the magnetic field distributions resulting from various magnetic sources placed close to the cell.

arxiv-2308-01907.title: The All-Seeing Project: Towards Panoptic Visual Recognition and Understanding of the Open World
arxiv-2308-01907.creator: Weiyun Wang, Min Shi, Qingyun Li, Wenhai Wang, Zhenhang Huang, Linjie Xing, Zhe Chen, Hao Li, Xizhou Zhu, Zhiguo Cao, Yushi Chen, Tong Lu, Jifeng Dai, Yu Qiao
arxiv-2308-01907.description: Abstract We present the All-Seeing (AS) 1 1 1 “All-Seeing” is derived from “The All-Seeing Eye”, which means having complete knowledge, awareness, or insight into all aspects of existence. project: a large-scale data and model for recognizing and understanding everything in the open world.

arxiv-2405-12255.title: Mammo-CLIP: A Vision Language Foundation Model to Enhance Data Efficiency and Robustness in Mammography
arxiv-2405-12255.creator: Shantanu Ghosh ( ✉ ) {}^{(\textrm{{\char 0\relax}})}, Clare B. Poynton, Shyam Visweswaran, Kayhan Batmanghelich
arxiv-2405-12255.description: Abstract The lack of large and diverse training data on Computer-Aided Diagnosis (CAD) in breast cancer detection has been one of the concerns that impedes the adoption of the system. Recently, pre-training with large-scale image text datasets via Vision-Language models (VLM) ( e.g., CLIP) partially addresses the issue of robustness and data efficiency in computer vision (CV).

arxiv-2507-19774.title: Bag of Coins: A Statistical Probe into Neural Confidence Structures
arxiv-2507-19774.creator: Agnideep Aich, Ashit Baran Aich, Md Monzur Murshed, Sameera Hewage, Bruce Wade
arxiv-2507-19774.description: Abstract Modern neural networks, despite their high accuracy, often produce poorly calibrated confidence scores, limiting their reliability in high-stakes applications. Existing calibration methods typically post-process model outputs without interrogating the internal consistency of the predictions themselves. In this work, we introduce a novel, non-parametric statistical probe, the Bag-of-Coins (BoC) test, that examines the internal consistency of a classifier’s logits.

arxiv-2508-02513.title: Modular Arithmetic: Language Models Solve Math Digit by Digit
arxiv-2508-02513.creator: Tanja Baeumel Daniil Gurgurov Yusser Al Ghussin Josef van Genabith Simon Ostermann
arxiv-2508-02513.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tanja Baeumel Daniil Gurgurov Yusser Al Ghussin Josef van Genabith Simon Ostermann. While recent work has begun to uncover the internal strategies that Large Language Models (LLMs) employ for simple arithmetic tasks, a unified understanding of their underlying mechanisms is still lacking. We extend recent findings showing that LLMs represent numbers in a digit-wise manner and present evidence for the existence of digit-position-specific circuits that LLMs use to perform simple arithmetic tasks, i.e.

arxiv-2509-14959.title: Discrete optimal transport is a strong audio adversarial attack
arxiv-2509-14959.creator: A. Selitskiy, A. Shahriyar, J. Prakasan
arxiv-2509-14959.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. Selitskiy, A. Shahriyar, J. Prakasan. In this paper, we show that discrete optimal transport (DOT) is an effective black-box adversarial attack against modern audio anti-spoofing countermeasures (CMs). Our attack operates as a post-processing, distribution-alignment step: frame-level WavLM embeddings of generated speech are aligned to an unpaired bona fide pool via entropic OT and a top- k k barycentric projection, then decoded with a neural vocoder.

arxiv-2601-13193.title: Asymptotic Stability of Rarefaction Waves for the Hyperbolized Navier-Stokes-Fourier System Thanks: Yuxi Hu, Department of Mathematics, China University of Mining and Technology, Beijing, 100083 and Key Laboratory of Scientific and Engineering Computing (Ministry of Education), P.R. China, yxhu86@16
arxiv-2601-13193.creator: Yuxi Hu, Mengran Yuan and Jie Zhang
arxiv-2601-13193.description: Abstract . This paper investigates the asymptotic stability of rarefaction waves for a one-dimensional compressible fluid system, where the Newton’s law of viscosity and Fourier’s law of heat conduction are replaced by Maxwell’s law and Cattaneo’s law, respectively. The system, which generalizes the classical Navier-Stokes-Fourier equations, features finite signal propagation speeds.

However, NIPP is not yet well established in dentistry, although it has promising potential, especially for periodontological applications.

pmc-11328534.title: Development of a text mining algorithm for identifying adverse drug reactions in electronic health records
pmc-11328534.creator: Britt W M van de Burgt, Arthur T M Wasylewicz, Bjorn Dullemond, Naomi T Jessurun, Rene J E Grouls, R Arthur Bouwman, Erik H M Korsten, Toine C G Egberts
pmc-11328534.description: ObjectiveAdverse drug reactions (ADRs) are a significant healthcare concern. They are often documented as free text in electronic health records (EHRs), making them challenging to use in clinical decision support systems (CDSS). The study aimed to develop a text mining algorithm to identify ADRs in free text of Dutch EHRs.

pmc-11613364.title: Mentor-Mentee relationship in Medicine: How to develop trust?
pmc-11613364.creator: Khadijah Mukhtar, Mahnoor Mukhtar, Syed Abdullah Haider, Sadia Iram
pmc-11613364.description: A mentor-mentee relationship, also known as a mentoring relationship, is a professional or personal partnership in which a more experienced or knowledgeable individual (the mentor) provides guidance, support, and advice to a less experienced or knowledgeable individual (the mentee). The primary purpose of this relationship is to facilitate the mentee’s personal and professional growth.

pmc-12698069.title: Pontine Tegmental Cap Dysplasia: A Rare Case in South Africa
pmc-12698069.creator: Thobeka Nyila, Gopolang Mndebele, Nonceba Koranteng, Gary Peiser
pmc-12698069.description: We present the first case of pontine tegmental cap dysplasia (PTCD) reported in South Africa, involving a one-year-old girl with bilateral sensorineural deafness, global atrophy, hemivertebrae, and butterfly vertebrae. Clinical examination revealed subtle dysmorphic features, abnormal corneal sensation, bilateral strabismus, and uncertain visual acuity.

pmc-12847870.title: PIM kinase inhibition attenuates pro-tumoral and immunosuppressive functions of macrophages in classic Hodgkin lymphoma
pmc-12847870.creator: Maciej Szydłowski, Ewa Kurtz, Filip Garbicz, Julia Maroszek, Michał Pawlak, Natalia Ochocka, Marcin Tabaka, Monika Prochorec-Sobieszek, Anna Szumera-Ciećkiewicz, Patryk Górniak, Olga Szymańska-Giemza, Grzegorz Rymkiewicz, Agnieszka Kołkowska-Leśniak, Wojciech Kukwa, Ewa Paszkiewicz-Kozik, Justyna To
pmc-12847870.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) of classic Hodgkin Lymphoma (cHL) contribute to the development of immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and are associated with worse treatment outcomes. However, detailed features, functions and therapeutic vulnerabilities of cHL TAMs remain largely unknown. To address this, we analyzed cHL diagnostic biopsies by Cellular Indexing of Transcriptomes and Epitopes by Sequencing (CITE-seq) and assessed transcriptional, proteomic and metabolic profiles of in vitro TAM models.

pmc-13300277.title: Perceived Exertion Is Associated with Cardiovascular Strain but Not Glycemic Response to Gym-Based Exercise in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes: An Exploratory Randomized Crossover Trial
pmc-13300277.creator: José Adevalton Feitosa Gomes, Anthony Rodrigues de Vasconcelos, José Roberto Andrade do Nascimento Júnior, Ysadora Verena Ribeiro de Souza, Fabiana Oliveira dos Santos Camatari, Bruno Bavaresco Gambassi, Manoel da Cunha Costa, Paulo Adriano Schwingel, Jorge Luiz de Brito Gomes
pmc-13300277.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Highlights Public health relevance—How does this work relate to a public health issue? Adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) carry an elevated cardiovascular risk profile, and regular exercise is a cornerstone non-pharmacological strategy to mitigate this risk.In real-world gym settings, however, continuous cardiovascular and glycemic monitoring is rarely available, limiting the safe and effective implementation of exercise prescriptions in this at-risk population. Public health significance—Why is this work of significance to public health?

pmc-13355716.title: Effects of spirulina powder on the physicochemical and volatile properties of rice bahlls
pmc-13355716.creator: Xiwu Jia, Yujun Shi, Zhili Ji, Wangyang Shen, Xin Liu, Bo Yu, Yolani Syaputri, Hongjian Zhang
pmc-13355716.description: This study compared the quality of rice balls prepared with different concentrations of spirulina powder (0%, 1%, 3%, 5%, and 7%) and investigated their nutritional composition, color parameters, hardness, water distribution, and fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) findings.

pmc-13356807.title: Oral cancer large observational screening study in Hungary
pmc-13356807.creator: Edit Marosi, István Kenessey, Éva Székelyhidi, Katalin Nagy, Ferenc Oberna, Zoltán Takácsi-Nagy, András Wéber, Csilla Egri Árváné, Renáta Tamás Bertókné, Orsolya Surján, Péter Nagy, Cecília Müller
pmc-13356807.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Incidence and mortality of oral cancer slightly decreased in recent years in Hungary; however, age-standardized estimated incidence and mortality for both sexes are still among the highest in Europe. The objective of the large observational study was to conduct oral cancer screening in Hungary using mobile screening units to examine 5000 individuals living in converging municipalities with low population density and under challenging socio-economic conditions.

pmc-13379695.title: Integrative Traditional East Asian Medicine–Based Adjunctive Therapies for Patients With Prostate Cancer Undergoing Standard Cancer Treatment: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
pmc-13379695.creator: So-Jeong Wi, Dong-Hyeon Kim, Su-Hyon Kim, Sang-Jin Lee, Jong-Sung Park, Seon-Mi Shin, Byung-Cheol Lee, So-Jung Park, Javad Sarvestan, Soo-Dam Kim, Rashad Ismayilov
pmc-13379695.description: BackgroundProstate cancer treatment increasingly emphasizes quality-of-life maintenance alongside oncological control. Integrative Traditional East Asian Medicine (TEAM), including traditional Chinese medicine, traditional Korean medicine, and Kampo medicine, has been used as an adjunctive approach for symptom management during cancer treatment. However, evidence regarding its effectiveness and safety across different disease stages remains heterogeneous and has not been comprehensively synthesized.

pmc-13445680.title: Migraine phases and treatment response: a post hoc analysis of participants with migraine with aura from the TEAM study
pmc-13445680.creator: Michael A. L. Johnson, Gregory Panza, Deena E. Kuruvilla
pmc-13445680.description: BackgroundMigraine is a phased neurological disorder progressing through prodrome, aura (in approximately one-third of patients), headache, and postdrome. Migraine with aura (MA) and migraine without aura (MO) are pathophysiologically distinct subtypes with potentially different treatment responses. Some acute therapies, including triptans, show reduced efficacy when administered during the aura phase. Whether this extends to neuromodulation remains unclear.

pmc-13471232.title: Citrullination-associated transcriptional states identify a non-canonical invasive program in malignant epithelial cells and correlate with SPP1-CD44 immune microenvironment niches in thyroid cancer
pmc-13471232.creator: Zhisheng Tian, Peiling Zhu, Xiujuan Zhao, Fan Yang
pmc-13471232.description: Highlights•Single-cell atlas reveals citrullination-enriched malignant states in thyroid cancer.•High-citrullination cells adopt a non-canonical high-invasion/high-apoptosis program.•The C_core program exhibits druggable CDC37-HSP90-PI3K/MAPK vulnerabilities.•CD44 is a functional hub linking macrophage communication to malignant maintenance. Introduction Thyroid cancer is the most common endocrine cancer worldwide. Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) constitutes 85–90% of cases and is generally associated with an excellent prognosis [1].
